target_customer: Informal-sector transport operators, passengers, merchants and institutions in Nigeria/Africa
problem: Cash-based micro-transactions (e.g. bus fares) in Africa's informal sector are untracked and leak revenue.
business_model: Transaction processing with NFC cards (Cowry card) and apps; fees likely (unverified)

founders.name: Michael Oluwole
founders.background_notes: Mechanical engineering, business process development and project management per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: NFC hardware cards working offline plus payment app and merchant integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Deployments with transport unions could be sticky; unsourced.

market_need_then: Company says it helps over 300k people pay bus fares digitally; cash dominates informal transport. No independent dated source.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Making life easier for africans one TAP at a time

branding.brand_signature: Cowry card (named after the traditional shell currency)

outcome_analysis: Touch and Pay Technologies (Winter 2022) is still active with 55 staff and claims 300k+ users of its cash-microtransaction digitisation, expanding into health, identity and events products. No funding, competitor or outcome information was found in the sources reached.
notes: The Cowry name's link to the cowry shell is my inference from the name and is not stated by a source; treat as unsourced.
